actions.summary: Information scrambling, characterized by the growth of operator entanglement and OTOCs, effectively delocalizes quantum information across many-body degrees of freedom. However, this process does not preclude the emergence of objective records, provided that environmental interactions (decoherence) enable the formation of Spectrum Broadcast Structures (SBS) or equivalent redundant encodings of system pointer states. Evidence confirms that scrambling dynamics and SBS formation are distinct operational signatures; scrambling measures the spread of information, while SBS measures the accessibility of information to multiple observers.
actions.title: Information Scrambling and Record Accessibility
